# `lib/substring.x`

Borrowed immutable views of String bytes.

## Primary API

| Function | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`String.substring`](#String.substring) | Returns a borrowed immutable view of the requested byte range. |
| [`Substring.compare`](#Substring.compare) | Compares contents in bytewise lexical order. |
| [`Substring.equal`](#Substring.equal) | Compares contents without materializing either view. |
| [`Substring.hash`](#Substring.hash) | Hashes the referenced bytes, independent of their source or offset. |
| [`Substring.len`](#Substring.len) | Returns the byte length without allocating. |
| [`Substring.new`](#Substring.new) | Borrows length bytes at offset. |
| [`Substring.str`](#Substring.str) | Materializes a canonical String in the active pool. |
| [`Substring.string`](#Substring.string) | Materializes the same canonical String as str(). |
| [`Substring.try_next`](#Substring.try_next) | Yields the next word view. |

#### Substring.str

`String Substring.str(Substring view)`

Materializes a canonical String in the active pool. Repeated conversion

<a id="Substring.try_next"></a>
#### Substring.try_next

`int Substring.try_next(String source, int &cursor, Substring &out)`

Yields the next word view. Start the caller-owned cursor at zero. The
source must stay live; exhaustion leaves cursor and out unchanged.
foreach (Substr word in source) uses this allocation-free cursor.

Source: `lib/substring.x:70`

<a id="Substring"></a>
### Substring

`typedef struct Substring { String source; int offset, length; } Substring`

A borrowed immutable range of a String. Assignment copies the view and
allocates nothing. Keep the source alive and unchanged through every use;
use str() or string() to obtain a canonical String in the active pool.
Construct views through Substring.new or String.substring.

Source: `lib/substring.x:11`
